title: LXC 111: implement the Palworld settings capability (read/write the server's own settings file)
description:
On LXC 111, add a backend route that reads and writes the Palworld server's settings (switches etc.) by editing the Palworld config file at PALWORLD_IP 192.168.1.106 over SSH as PALWORLD_USER aedefruscio, exposing GET/PUT of the settings keys. No UI yet. On container 111.

[Engine split of ADD100 — 2 of 8] Done when the capability WORKS, not when its code exists (operator decision 2026-10-07): `pct exec 111 -- curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/palworld-settings` returns the server's real settings including `ServerName` (from the live /opt/palworld/Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/PalWorldSettings.ini, or from /opt/palworld/DefaultPalWorldSettings.ini while the live file is empty); AND the block PUTs the CURRENT ServerName back unchanged through that same route (a write that changes nothing), after which `qm guest exec 106 -- grep -c OptionSettings= /opt/palworld/Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/PalWorldSettings.ini` answers 1 and the next GET still returns the same ServerName. (The path follows the capability registry that ADD121 built: /opt/control-panel-backend/config/capabilities.json gives this capability the id `palworld-settings`.)
